These source observations do not prove that the native call reads that table or returns its value; assignment ORDER is proved inside the init chain: globallogic.gsc:187 sets level.teambased = 0 FIRST, then globallogic.gsc:198 calls gametype::init(), which first reads bundle15 and returns19-22 if undefined. Only a defined bundle reaches the native builtin/write24; if missing, the earlier0 survives this chain. With a defined bundle and a returning call, the later assignment uses that opaque result. An effective HMH true value is conditional on an unverified mapping between the recovered table and the native call; neither native internal reads nor its actual result are established. (3) teamcount â€” globallogic.gsc:188 level.teamcount = getgametypesetting(#teamcount); the compared recovered HMH layer rules contain no explicit identified #teamcount name. That literal observation does not establish semantic key absence: opaque hash-named fields/settings, native/online layers and store merging remain unresolved.
